reason: The cited evidence shows CALPHAD's general capability for phase prediction (E1) and that third-generation descriptions improve binary assessments (E3), but none of the passages provide specific prior evidence that such an integrated framework has already achieved the claimed 5–10% accuracy for melting temperatures, fusion enthalpies/entropies, or volume changes across HEAs. The fusion data example in E2 is for rare earth oxides, not HEAs, and does not demonstrate the proposed predictive performance.
premises: CALPHAD can predict phase stability in multi-component alloys by minimizing Gibbs free energy
Third-generation Gibbs energy descriptions improve accuracy for pure elements and binaries down to 0 K
Fusion enthalpies and volume changes can be incorporated into CALPHAD assessments from experimental data
Reliable binary/ternary thermodynamic assessments are available for some high-entropy alloy systems
Integrated CALPHAD models can predict melting temperatures and fusion properties within ~5–10% error
